Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zupmxio 0.0.0.9000

  • Readers refuse more models whose meaning they could not keep:

    • a name reassigned after a derivative, dosing attribute or scale reads it, whose value the representation could not hold (#146);
    • a format’s built-in names (NEWIND, ICALL, EVID, tad, …) read as covariates, and NM-TRAN’s CALLFL (#149); pi, M_PI and C++ true and false read as numbers;
    • omega and sigma blocks that are not positive semi-definite (#150);
    • a NONMEM ODE model scaling a compartment it does not observe, since without DEFOBS NONMEM observes compartment 1 (#148);
    • an undeclared EPS(n) in a residual model (#30), unknown mrgsolve @options (#154), and $PKMODEL advan = 2.9 (#155).

  • pmx_write_nonmem() marks the observed compartment of an ODE model with DEFOBS (#148), and pmx_write_rxode2() writes ADVAN12 under names rxode2 simulates (#176).

  • pmx_read_mrgsolve() reads $INIT compartments (#153), $PARAM @covariates (#154) and multi-line /* */ comments (#68).

  • pmx_compare() simulates a model’s own rxode2 function or mrgsolve file when it can (#170), keeps the caller’s random numbers (#162), matches the endpoint column exactly (#152), and documents the errors it raises (#163). Against tables, each value keeps its own printed precision, so a fixed-format small value no longer loosens the rest (#147); EVID 2 records reach the engines (#169); and tables without observations fail with a reason (#156).

  • pmx_read_json() raises only parse errors for malformed documents (#151).

  • The package is renamed zupmxio, from zufapmx (design D24). Condition classes are zupmxio_*_error and the corpus is zupmxio_corpus(); the pmx_* functions keep their names.

  • pmx_compare() checks that two models are the same model. It simulates both on a pmx_design() (single dose, infusion, multiple doses and steady state, for a typical subject and n subjects with random effects), each through its own engine and never on the engine of the writer under test, and compares the predictions point by point. A failed comparison is a value that says where the models differ. pmx_report() writes a comparison as Markdown, with both model texts.

  • Reading a control stream is about twice as fast: the NM-TRAN and C++ tokenizers match all their patterns in one pass per line.

  • pmx_read_tables() reads NONMEM $TABLE output, and pmx_compare(tables, model) checks a translation against the run’s own PRED: the model’s typical subject is simulated on the tables’ records and compared within the precision NONMEM printed.

  • pmx_write_json() and pmx_read_json() write the representation as JSON and read it back unchanged (needs zujson).

  • pmx_write_rxode2() writes NONMEM’s combined residual IPRED * (1 + EPS(1)) + EPS(2), which it refused (#129), and writers no longer fail on a closed-form parameter assigned from a covariate (#130).

  • pmx_write_mrgsolve() declares covariates in $INPUT, without a default value, so its output compiles; pmx_read_mrgsolve() reads $INPUT names as covariates (#126).

  • Models follow one rule for who may assign and read what (design D18): parameters, random effects, compartments and time are never assigned, ODE code does not reassign individual parameters, and individual statements do not read compartment amounts. The rxode2 reader moves statements into the ODE code until that holds, and keeps an endpoint that other statements read as a statement.

  • Readers refuse more constructs that would change predictions: a Y reassigned or set inside IF, a scale or dosing attribute assigned twice, TSCALE, XSCALE, INITIALOFF, code after a plain ELSE, fractional compartment indices, $ODE beside $PKMODEL, time from the wrong record (TIME in $DES, SOLVERTIME outside $ODE), $NMXML and $NMEXT options the reader does not honour, C++ integer division of comparisons, and rxode2’s combined1().

  • A NONMEM Y that does not use F, as in IPRED = A(2)/V, gives its own prediction instead of the compartment amount.

  • A refusal of a statement points at its record’s first line, and a writer’s refusal lists only formats that do write the model.

  • pmx_write_nonmem() lists the model’s covariates in $INPUT. Writers record lost bounds on residual standard deviations, and pmx_read_mrgsolve() records $PARAM values written as expressions.

  • pmx_read_rxode2() accepts = in ini() and combined2().

  • An invalid argument is a zupmxio_model_error with one wording across functions, and a model edited after reading is validated again before it is written or inspected.

  • Fidelity is stricter: a write is "equivalent" only through the reparameterisations writers are known to make, and a translation that reads back as a different model is a zupmxio_write_error.

  • Time is one symbol, t, read from and written to each format’s own spelling (NONMEM TIME/T, mrgsolve TIME/SOLVERTIME, rxode2 t/time). Free names are recorded as covariates in a model’s provenance.

  • Readers refuse more of what they cannot translate faithfully (dosing assignments inside IF, undeclared THETA/ETA/EPS, C++ integer division) and accept more of what they can ($PKMODEL over $PARAM, $SIZES, record options, statement-defined residual parameters).

  • pmx_read_mrgsolve() reads an mrgsolve model file and pmx_write_mrgsolve() writes one.

  • pmx_write_nonmem() writes a NONMEM control stream.

  • pmx_read_nonmem() reads a NONMEM control stream, with final estimates from run.xml, the .ext file or the .lst report.

  • pmx_read_rxode2() reads an rxode2 or nlmixr2 model function and pmx_write_rxode2() writes one. pmx_fidelity() and pmx_losses() say how faithful a written model is.

  • pmx_parameters(), pmx_omega() and pmx_ode() inspect a model, and print() summarises it.

  • zupmxio_corpus() lists the shipped model corpus: one-, two- and three-compartment closed-form models and a Michaelis-Menten ODE model, each written in NONMEM, rxode2 and mrgsolve form with its typical-subject predictions.

  • Initial CRAN submission.
